items.title: The Third Cat

Also, Casey's line appeared after the day had ended, which looks like an app ordering bug. Fix: require a minimum number of beats before CAW counts, and avoid giving the same player Meowfia in back-to-back rounds.

items.title: The Top Cat Flips

items.text: Casey, round 3: Casey claimed that throwing at Alex 'may decide nothing' because Alex was already dead from a failed Coon bet. Ellis and Finley said it was a guaranteed win. The rules don't say whether a player who lost exclusively can be eggsecuted, or what that would mean for Farm, so nobody could settle it.

items.text: In a one-round game, losing on your own team costs everything thrown. Ellis lost 43 points and Blair won by 33. A single misread vote decides the whole game. Consider playing more rounds, or giving a small floor for losers.

items.text: Blair, round 1: Blair said the 5 eggs were 'capped'. Casey's nest held exactly 5, so the cap never applied. This is minor.

changes.title: Tell a hugged player (6.8)
changes.hypothesis: Fewer honest Farm players are eggsecuted because of a hug they were not told about

changes.title: Egg tokens, cashed after the vote (6.6)
changes.hypothesis: The table reads the round better when nest counts are exact and confusion moves no cards

changes.title: Open vote, trial, then stake (6.5)
changes.hypothesis: The vote is a real choice between two: more candidates share the vote

changes.title: The cats see each other, with safe claims (6.4)
changes.hypothesis: Cats who know each other stop hitting each other; Farm wins less

changes.title: Secret score piles (6.7)
changes.hypothesis: Nobody can vote against the leader: the leader-hunting exploiter wins less

changes.title: A stake of at most three cards (6.3)
changes.hypothesis: No single round outweighs the others: the winner gets less of the score from their best round

changes.title: The stake pays on your own read (6.2)
changes.hypothesis: A correct read is paid: accuracy explains more of a winner points; the sides even out

changes.title: One player, one vote (6.1)
changes.hypothesis: Largest single share of the vote falls; fewer rounds decided by one throw

changes.title: Nest sizes show their change
changes.detail: The day's list of nest sizes gives each nest's change since this round's deal, because nests carry over between rounds and players were reading leftover cards as last night's eggs.

changes.title: Golden Wattle: answer at once
changes.detail: A player offered a handshake must accept or decline there and then.

changes.title: The Goose needs a player
changes.detail: Scoring is inverted only when a player is the Goose; each Goose inverts it once.

changes.title: The pool is the chosen cards
changes.detail: Every chosen animal is in the pool from round one; nothing is revealed during the game. A set number of the chosen flowers are picked at random and stay all game unless their card says to discard them.

changes.title: First place is the goal
changes.detail: The rules say only first place wins and spell out the pull between team and self. Scores are announced at the start of each round. A seat can be given a temperament.

changes.title: Crimson Kunzea: the early vote
changes.detail: Doubling down means throwing your eggs at a player there and then, in the open, as your vote.

changes.title: Meowfia count by table size
changes.detail: 1 Meowfia at four players, 1 or 2 at five or six, 2 or 3 at seven or eight, instead of a 33% roll. Messages over the word limit end at a full sentence.

changes.title: Live talk: word clock and exchanges
changes.detail: The day is a clock of spoken words, messages are short, two players can go back and forth, and CAW CAW counts without the floor.

changes.title: Live talk: bidding for the floor
changes.detail: After every message each player bids 0 to 3 to speak next; naming a player favours them.

changes.detail: A second discussion system, live talk, and a basics-only setup for testing.
